先聽弦樂的起音。腸弦的起音比鋼弦軟，音符之間有比較明顯的空間。: Start with the attack of the strings. A gut string's attack is softer than a steel string's, and there is more audible space between the notes.
古樂合奏團（Period-Instrument Ensemble）— 以歷史樂器: Period-Instrument Ensemble — a body that rebuilds the sound of old works with historical instruments, a lower pitch standard and valveless brass. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
古樂合奏團（period-instrument ensemble）是用與作品同時: A period-instrument ensemble performs old works on instruments of the same period or of an earlier build, following the playing conventions of the time. Its point is not playing old music — every classical ensemble plays old music — but deliberately changing the instruments and the pitch standard so that the balance of the sound returns to what it was when the score was written.
古樂團不用指揮，所以速度很自由。: Period groups have no conductor, so the tempo is free.
古樂團也改變了「什麼算好聽」的標準。現代樂團追求融合、均勻、飽滿；古樂團則容許更: Period groups also change the standard for what counts as good sound. Modern orchestras aim for blend, evenness and fullness; period ensembles allow far more breaks in timbre and far more asymmetry. The uneven tuning of woodwind fingerholes, the notes that must be stopped on a natural horn, the noise in a gut string's attack — under modern standards these are faults; in the logic of early music they are part of each instrument's character. To judge a period ensemble you do not listen for how clean it is but for whether it turns those limits into music.
古樂團出現在音樂廳的古樂系列、教堂、音樂節、歌劇院與錄音。曲目以文藝復興到古典時: Period ensembles appear in concert-hall early-music series, churches, festivals, opera houses and recordings. The repertoire runs mainly from the Renaissance to the classical period, but reaches into the early nineteenth century — as long as the instruments and the conventions still line up. In recent years some period ensembles have played Romantic works, or recorded film scores on historical instruments.
古樂團就是比較小聲、比較柔的管弦樂團。: A period ensemble is just a quieter, softer orchestra.
古樂團最直接的差異是音高標準。現代樂團多把 A 定在 440 或 442 Hz；: The most direct difference is the pitch standard. Modern orchestras mostly set A at 440 or 442 Hz; period ensembles often set A at around 415 Hz, roughly a semitone below modern pitch. Why 415? Because it falls inside the range of ensemble pitches used in some places and settings in the baroque era, and because it sits exactly a semitone below modern pitch, which makes swapping between period and modern groups easiest. The lower pitch is not there to sound deeper; it acts directly on string tension. At the same note, a lower frequency lets the string be thinner and less tense, so the sound is looser and less strained. The whole band plays under lower tension, and the sense of pressure in the sound is different.
古樂團的指揮模式也比較自由：小型編制常由首席用弓或身體帶拍，大鍵琴手也用右手帶拍: Period ensembles are also freer about how they are directed: small line-ups are often led by the leader with the bow or the body, and the harpsichordist beats with the right hand. With no conductor, the quartet's logic of negotiation is scaled up to the whole band — the tempo comes from the leader and the bass listening to each other.

古樂團聽起來比較「正確」，因為它還原了作曲家的原意。: Period groups sound more correct, because they restore what the composer intended.
古樂團還原的是樂器與音高的物理條件，不是作曲家的意圖。同一個時代、同一個城市，音: What a period ensemble restores is the physical condition of instruments and pitch, not the composer's intention. In one era and one city there was more than one pitch standard and more than one instrument build; a correct version does not exist.
和現代室內樂團的差別在「歷史」是不是核心。現代室內樂團可以用現代樂器演奏任何時期: The difference from a modern chamber ensemble is whether history is the point. A modern chamber ensemble can play any period on modern instruments; a period ensemble is defined by the historicalness of its instruments and conventions, and once you put modern instruments in its hands it is no longer a period ensemble.
大鍵琴（harpsichord）、管風琴、低音管、大提琴、低音提琴: Harpsichord, organ, bassoon, cello, double bass
它的音量分布不同：弦樂較小、木管相對前面、銅管有音色斷層。這是一套不同的平衡，不: Its volume is distributed differently: the strings are smaller, the woodwinds sit relatively forward, and the brass has breaks in its timbre. This is a different balance, not a scaled-down copy of the same one.
常由首席、大鍵琴手或低音提琴手帶拍，不一定有指揮: Often directed from the leader, the harpsichordist or the double bass; not necessarily conducted
提供和聲的根音與數字低音（basso continuo）的實現，也提供節奏的硬度: Supplies the roots of the harmony and the realisation of the figured bass (basso continuo), and gives the rhythm its hardness
最常被對比的是現代管弦樂團。兩者的曲目大量重疊，差別在樂器與音高基準：古樂團用腸: The usual comparison is the modern orchestra. The two repertoires overlap heavily; the difference is instruments and pitch standard: gut strings, valveless brass and a lower A against steel strings, valved brass and 440 or 442. In sound the period strings are thinner, the woodwinds sit further forward and the brass has breaks in its timbre.
樂器的選擇不是為了「聽起來比較老」，而是為了改變平衡。腸弦的張力低、音量小、泛音: The instruments are not chosen to sound older but to change the balance. Gut strings have low tension, little volume and few overtones, so the strings do not bury the woodwinds the way a modern orchestra's do; the woodwinds then need no protecting and can return to the proportion they actually had in the eighteenth century. The band's balance grows out of the physics of the instruments rather than being pressed out by a conductor.
比較同一首曲子在古樂團與現代樂團的版本。速度、音高、樂器音色都不同，差別比想像中: Compare the same piece played by a period ensemble and a modern orchestra. Tempo, pitch and instrumental timbre all differ, and the gap is wider than you would expect.
沒有指揮時，速度由首席與低音聲部協商，反而更需要固定的排練共識。自由是排練出來的: With no conductor, tempo is negotiated between the leader and the bass, which makes a fixed rehearsal consensus more necessary, not less. The freedom is rehearsed, not improvised on the night.
注意大鍵琴的低音。它不只彈和聲，也提供節奏的硬度，常常是整個團的脈搏。: Listen to the harpsichord's bass. It does not only play the harmony; it gives the rhythm its hardness, and it is often the pulse of the whole band.
無閥銅管是第三個差異。自然號只能吹出泛音列上的音，其他音要靠右手伸進喇叭口、半閉: Valveless brass is the third difference. A natural horn can only play the notes of the harmonic series; for the rest the player puts the right hand into the bell and half-stops it to raise the pitch by about a semitone (hand stopping), or lips the note up. That means the brass in old works is never asked to play any note at all but to pick the notes the harmonic series offers. What composers wrote for the natural horn therefore has its own melodic shapes and harmonic habits. Listening to the brass in a period ensemble you hear clear breaks in timbre: within one part some notes are open, others are stopped by the hand and turn stuffy — the instrument's limits written straight into the music.
無閥，只能吹泛音列上的音；其他音靠手塞（hand stopping）或更換接管（: Valveless, so only the notes of the harmonic series; the rest come from hand stopping or from changing the crook
編制規模也不一樣。古樂團通常比現代管弦樂團小，弦樂聲部常常只有幾個人，木管每種一: The size of the band differs too. A period ensemble is usually smaller than a modern orchestra: the string sections often have only a few players, the woodwinds one or two of each, the brass fewer still. The small size lets every player be heard and makes chamber-style listening possible — players are not hiding inside a section but listening to each other like a quartet. This difference of scale directly shapes the period ensemble's dynamics and flexibility: it can make the fine tempo changes a large modern band cannot.
聽木管與弦樂的比例。古樂團的木管通常比現代樂團更前面，不會被弦樂蓋住。: Listen to the balance between woodwinds and strings. Period woodwinds usually sit further forward than in a modern orchestra and are not covered by the strings.
聽自然號的音色斷層。同一個聲部裡，有的音開闊、有的音悶，這是無閥樂器的限制。: Listen for the breaks in the natural horn's timbre. Within one part some notes are open and others stuffy; that is the limit of a valveless instrument.
腸弦是第二個差異。現代小提琴用鋼弦，音量大、泛音亮、音準穩定；腸弦的聲音集中在比: Gut strings are the second difference. A modern violin uses steel strings: louder, with bright overtones and stable intonation. A gut string concentrates its sound in the lower overtones, has a soft attack and a short decay. That changes the strings' role in the ensemble: no longer a thick wall but a textured line. The woodwinds can then be heard, and the brass does not need to be pushed to its limit.
與室內樂式的古樂組合（例如古樂四重奏、魯特琴歌曲伴奏）相比，差別在規模與低音持續: Compared with a chamber-scale period group (a period quartet, say, or a lute accompanying songs), the difference is scale and how the continuo is staffed. A small period group often realises the harmony on a harpsichord or a lute alone; a period ensemble builds a bass group from harpsichord, cello and bassoon, which gives the harmony a different density and weight.
裝飾音也牽涉到即興。巴洛克與古典時期的裝飾音，很多時候譜上只有一個符號，實際要演: Ornamentation involves improvisation too. In baroque and classical music an ornament is often just a sign on the page, and what it is actually played as is up to the performer. The same sign draws different figures, different note values and different accent positions from different players. This improvisation is not free invention but a choice inside a stylistic frame, and the edges of that frame are exactly what period research is about.
這種模式改變了排練的內容。現代樂團的排練多半是「指揮解決問題」：哪裡不齊、哪裡太: This way of working changes what rehearsal is for. A modern orchestra mostly rehearses by the conductor solving problems: something is not together, something is too loud, and the conductor fixes it with words and gestures. A period ensemble's rehearsal is closer to building a version together: how to ornament, how to staff the continuo, where the phrase breathes — all of it discussed. Players are expected to bring their own ideas rather than wait for instructions.
還有一個常被忽略的層面：低音持續（continuo）。巴洛克合奏的低音不是只有一: One layer is easily overlooked: the continuo. The bass of a baroque ensemble is not a single line but a group of players — harpsichord, cello, bassoon — filling in the harmony from the figured bass in real time. The harpsichordist reads a bass line with figures and decides the actual spacing of the chords on the spot. The same bass line therefore comes out at different harmonic densities from different harpsichordists. This is the part of a period ensemble closest to improvisation: the score gives the skeleton of bass and harmony, and the players fill in the actual sound as they go.
錄音也改變了古樂團的發展。二十世紀後半，古樂錄音從「學術示範」變成「市場產品」，: Recording changed how period ensembles developed as well. In the second half of the twentieth century period recordings went from academic demonstration to market product, and ensembles began to be expected to have a fixed sound and style. That had a side effect: to sound consistent on record, some period ensembles polish their intonation and timbre so smooth that the unevenness of the old instruments is lost. When you listen to period recordings, a live one usually keeps that unevenness better than a studio version.
鍵數較少，音準靠指法與嘴型，音色變化大: Fewer keys; intonation depends on fingering and embouchure, and the timbre varies widely
音律是另一個常被忽略的層面。古樂團常用的不是現代鋼琴的十二平均律，而是各種「微調: Temperament is another layer that is easily overlooked. Period ensembles usually do not use the equal temperament of the modern piano but some kind of adjusted system: some built on pure fifths, some making certain thirds especially pure and certain fifths especially narrow. These systems mean that intervals of the same name differ in quality from key to key — the same major third comes close to just intonation in some keys and sits narrow or wide in others. Period players have to adjust pitch as they play to make the chords sound pure, which is nothing like the modern orchestra's logic of every note being fixed. Keyboard instruments show it most clearly: once a harpsichord or organ is tuned, some keys sound especially beautiful and others especially harsh, and composers took that character of keys into account when they wrote.
音色比現代鋼弦暗、泛音少，聲音更靠中頻: Darker than modern steel strings, with fewer overtones; the sound sits closer to the midrange
